ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the radius of $\odot O$ is $\sqrt{5}$. AB and CD are two parallel chords of $\odot O$, with $\angle CDE=30^\circ$ and $AD=2$. What is the length of chord BE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OC, OE, BC, CE, and draw CH$\perp$BE intersecting BE at point H,\\
$\because$AB$\parallel$CD,\\
$\therefore$BC = AD = 2,\\
$\because$$\angle$CDE = $30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$COE= $60^\circ$, $\angle$CBE = $\angle$CDE = $30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$$\triangle$OCE is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$CE= $\sqrt{5}$, in $Rt\triangle BCH$,\\
$CH=\frac{1}{2}BC=1$\\
$\therefore$BH= $\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\sqrt{3}$, in $Rt\triangle$CEH\\
HE= $\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^2-1^2}=2$\\
$\therefore$BE=2+ $\sqrt{3}$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: BE=\boxed{2+\sqrt{3}}.

The inscribed angle ∠CDE subtends arc CE, so the central angle over CE is 60°, giving chord CE=2R sin 30°=sqrt(5). Now convert chord BC=2 into its central half-angle: if the central angle for BC is θ, then sin(θ/2)=BC/(2R)=1/sqrt(5), so cos(θ/2)=2/sqrt(5). Since B, C, E are consecutive along the circle in the image, the central angle for chord BE is θ+60°. Therefore BE=2R sin((θ+60°)/2)=2sqrt(5)[sin(θ/2)cos30°+cos(θ/2)sin30°]=2+sqrt(3).
